note:
Forty-seven measured regions resolve to 24 exhibit rows (12 figures, 12 grids) and 23 exclusions, unaccounted 0. Every exclusion is display mathematics: equation (1) on p5, equations (2)-(6) on p6, the 22x22 matrix (7) on p7, the rate definitions on p8, the eigenvector and eigenvalue on p9, the block transition matrix and (14)-(15) on p12, the English-only matrix on p13, the initial vector and similarity parameter on p14, the k-exponent modification (17) on p17, the rating model (18) on p18 and the weight-coefficient lines on pp19-20. The mathematics is typeset, not pasted - decimal points print as colons ('[k = 0:1]', '[when > 0:021]') and both eta glyphs have dropped out of the siting captions - yet `fig_extract.py` boxes it as a raster region anyway, so this paper is the batch's cleanest case of the detector counting equations as pictures.

What this paper adds to the lane. (1) The caption side rule now has a third direction: #146 and #147 put figure captions below and table captions above, #145 put both below, and #148 puts both below again, so 'tables above' is one paper's habit rather than a batch convention. (2) It is the first paper in the batch whose grids are mostly uncaptioned: seven of twelve grids carry neither a number nor a caption, being symbol and result tables announced by their own section heading. They still have to be recorded - a census of what was drawn cannot skip the grids without numbers - so their caption block is empty with caption_source 'none'. (3) Three printed tables are missing from the layout entirely: Table 2 on p15 and Tables 3 and 5 on p25 are native text tables with rules, and the region pass boxes only Table 4 on p25, because that one happened to be a raster object. They are invisible to the detector and are recorded here only in this note. (4) Three measured boxes cut across printed objects: the p25 box runs from Table 3's caption through Table 4 into Table 5's header, and the p20 and p21 boxes each hold one office grid plus four rows of the next one. (5) File the figures as one engine, three idioms: seven MATLAB line plots, two hand-laid transition graphs, two 2x5 plates and one pie chart - and one exhibit family the vocabulary has no name for, which is why Figure 6 is filed 'other' with a note.

Defects worth recording. Figure 2's caption prints 'Rate ( )' where the learning-rate symbol fell out. Figure 5's inline region labels are 5-6 pt. Figures 7 and 8 carry twenty-six-entry key boxes placed outside the axes and illegible at print size, and their bottom eighteen curves merge below 350 million. Figure 9 is captioned Birth Rate while every panel axis reads 'Death rate/%', and Figure 10's axes read the same, so the two plates cannot be told apart from their labels. Figures 11 and 12 truncate their y axis at 50, inflating every trend. Figure 11 labels fifteen languages against a caption promising ranks 6 to 16, which is eleven. Table 1 prints '?' in both non-native Japanese columns. Tables 6 and 7 share one caption word for word, with both eta glyphs missing so the weighting condition prints as '1 = 2; 2 = 3 = 1'. Table 8 prints Spain twice, 'Rassia' for Russia and 'Bengaladesh' for Bangladesh, with 17 to 19 significant digits. The Memo grid misspells Berlin as 'Beilin'. The section 2.1.1 symbol grid spends 'ii' on two different rates, the section 3.1.2 grid writes its own constraint with the subscript flipped ('[0 < p_ij < 1]' in the p_ji row), and the section 4.2 grid puts a unit on two rows and none on the other six. A red Chinese shop-watermark band crosses the running header on every page.

Section grammar. This paper draws its model before it uses it: the N=2 transition graph (Figure 1), the learning-rate correlation that fixes the model's parameter range (Figure 2), the parameter-free validation against 2017 (Table 1), the eight-state graph of the modified model (Figure 3), then the projections themselves (Figure 4), the migration scale (Figure 5), the non-native distribution (Figure 6), the two sensitivity runs (Figures 7 and 8), the siting grids with the 2017 and 2067 office results (uncaptioned, in the body), the economic substrate (Table 8), and finally four appendix plates (Figures 9-12) that carry the twenty-one language groups the body could not fit. Three symbol grids stand in front of the three model blocks and none of them is captioned. What is missing is any figure of the object the paper is nominally about: no map, no scatter, no density, nothing geographic in a paper whose title promises the location.
rules: Numbering is one colon grammar twice over - every figure caption prints 'Figure N:' and every captioned grid prints 'Table N:' with the same colon, no period and no roman - but only five of the paper's twelve grids carry a number at all: the three symbol grids of sections 2.1.1, 3.1.2 and 4.2, the two 4.3 office grids and both Memo grids are bare [caption.numbering].

Caption side follows exhibit kind without exception: all twelve figure captions print BELOW the artwork and all five captioned grids print BELOW their last rule, so this paper puts every caption at the foot - #145's convention, and the opposite of #146 and #147, whose tables carried theirs above [caption.position].

Caption length is one line almost everywhere: the twelve figure captions run 9 to 19 words and the five grid captions 9 to 15, print in roman sentence case with no full stop and no bold, and no caption anywhere states a unit, a conclusion or a numeric condition [caption.words].

Symbols reach the captions only on the figure side - three of them name a parameter ('When k=0.1', 'When k=10', 'Top 6 to 16 Language Groups') - while none of the five captioned grids names a variable, so a reader holding only the table captions cannot recover a single column heading's units or argument order [caption.variable_count].

Three captions are wrong at the level of the noun and one is empty where a symbol belongs: Figure 9 is captioned 'Birth Rate' while its own axes read 'Death rate/%', Table 7 repeats Table 6's caption word for word, Table 1 promises 'Projections' for columns that mix prediction with realisation, and Figure 2 prints 'Rate ( )' with the parameter dropped out of the brackets [caption.verbatim].

No caption prints a unit and no caption states a result; the units that exist in this paper live inside the artwork (axis titles) or inside two cells of the section 4.2 symbol grid ('(Unit: million)', '(Unit: ten billion USD)') [caption.units].
The drawing is one engine and three idioms: seven of the twelve figures are MATLAB line plots, two are hand-laid transition graphs, two are 2x5 panel plates and one is a pie chart [geometry.family].

Nothing in the paper is three-dimensional and nothing carries a colour scale - no surf plot, no heatmap, no contour - so every quantity is read off a position against a printed tick, and the twelve figures together contain no key legible at print size [geometry.three_d].

Keys are rare and never inside the frame: two figures (7 and 8) key their twenty-six curves in a bordered box placed OUTSIDE the plotting area at the upper right, seven figures (1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 11, 12) label their marks inline, and the other three carry no key and no labels - a single-trace plot and the two plates whose panels are titled instead [geometry.legend].

Panel grammar has exactly two states: a single frame, or a 2x5 grid of ten titled panels in the two appendix plates. Only those two use panels, they do not share axes - every panel repeats its own 'Time/year' and 'Death rate/%' titles - and no panel letter (a)/(b) exists anywhere in the paper [geometry.panel_count].

Shared axes are used zero times: every multi-panel exhibit repeats its full axis labels panel by panel, and every multi-curve exhibit carries one y scale for all curves, which is why the eighteen bottom curves of Figures 7 and 8 merge into a single band below 350 million [geometry.shared_axes].

Printed values are absent from every figure - no data labels, no annotated points, no value strip under the plots: the only printed numbers in the artwork are axis ticks, so the three figures that matter most (4, 7, 8) present their twenty-six curves as indistinguishable hairlines [geometry.printed_numbers].

Every grid in the paper is booktabs: three horizontal rules (top, below the header, bottom), no vertical rule at any cell boundary, no outer box, no zebra shading and no slanted corner cell - the style is invariant across twelve grids, including the four whose content reaches the layout as a raster rather than as vectors [table.rule_style].

Merged cells appear exactly once: Table 1's 'Language' cell spans both header rows while the four measure labels wrap inside the second row. No other grid merges a cell, and no grid prints a diagonal header [table.merged_cells].

Header depth is one row for eleven of the twelve grids; only Table 1 needs two, and only the 2017 and 2067 office grids add a body band - a rule above their 'Accumulated scores' totals row - which is the sole footer structure in the paper [table.header_rows].

Grid width splits by function, not by size: the single comparison grid (Table 1) is set at about 60 percent of the measure while the nineteen-row economic table (Table 8) and the seventeen-row symbol grid run the full measure, so the paper lets its widest tables run wide and only the one it wants read against prose wrap [table.width].

Decoration is absent on the grid side as completely as on the figure side: no grid is striped, none is turned into landscape, none continues onto a second page, and not one of the twelve prints a source line or a table note that reaches the text layer - the only note-like row in the paper is the closing line of the section 4.2 grid, and it is inside the raster [table.note_sentence].

Announcement is same-page for four cited rows and one page early for five: Figures 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 are named in the prose on the page before their artwork prints, while Figures 1, 2, 7 and Table 1 are cited on their own page, so this paper's habit is to lead its exhibits by a page [mention.lead_pages].

Fifteen of the twenty-four rows are never cited from the body at all - Figures 9 to 12 and the eleven uncaptioned or appendix grids - and every one of them sits either at the foot of a section or inside the appendices, reached only by the bare gestures 'See: Apendix B', 'See: Appendix A' and 'the data in 2013 is in Appendix A' [mention.count].

Citation vocabulary is a parenthetical rotation: eight of the nine cited rows are introduced by '(Figure N)' or '(Table N)' glued to the end of a sentence, and only Figure 3 gets a full as-shown-in construction ('Example graph ... is shown below (Figure 3)') [mention.lead_pattern].

Placement follows the argument down the page: thirteen rows sit in the top third, seven in the middle band and four at the foot, and the four foot cases are the third panel of the appendix plate, the section 2.1.1 symbol grid that closes its page and two grids that fill the bottom half of a page of tables [place.page_zone].

Exhibit density is where the work is: six model rows, one result row, two sensitivity runs and three symbol grids fill sections 2 and 3, four uncaptioned grids belong to the application section and its Memo, and the appendices hold eight rows - four grids and four plates - while the introduction, the strengths section and the references carry nothing at all [place.section_kind].

Twenty-three of the forty-seven measured boxes are not exhibits: every one of them is display mathematics - equations (1) to (18), the parameter blocks, the 22x22 and 44x44 matrices and the phi ratios - which the detector boxes as an image region although the maths is typeset rather than scanned, so the region pass reads this paper's equations as artwork and at the same time misses three of its printed tables [place.area_frac].

No caption is printed - the section heading above does that job. Its own defect is that the symbol 'ii' is spent on two different quantities, the annual birth rate and the annual death rate of native speakers, so the two rows cannot be told apart from the table alone. the section 3.1.2 additional-symbol grid, the paper's longest table: seventeen rows against two columns, booktabs, no verticals, no shading, no caption. Its row for p_ji prints the constraint as '0 < p_ij < 1', flipping the subscript inside its own parenthetical, and the argument order of d_ji (similarity of i and j) runs opposite to S_ji (learners of j from i) without either row saying so

the section 4.2 symbol grid for the office-siting model: eight rows, two columns, booktabs, no key and no caption, plus a closing line below the last rule that defines the j = 0 subscript. That line is inside the region's raster and never reaches the text layer, so note_sentence is left empty and the fact is recorded here only. Units are printed inside the description cells rather than in the header, and only on two of the eight rows ('(Unit: million)' and '(Unit: ten billion USD)'), so the other six silently inherit them. The measured box also swallows the '4.3 Calculating and Simplifying' heading below it

the 2017 office-siting result for six offices: six rows against two columns (Office location, Covering languages (Exclusive of English)) plus a totals row 'Accumulated scores 43.0' set off by its own rule - the only grid in the paper with a footer band. Uncaptioned; the ranking lives in the prose. The measured box cuts the five-office table printed directly beneath it after four rows, so the region is one table plus a fragment of the next, and the language cells carry lower-case 'marathi' and spaces before commas ('Arabic ,Russian ,Bengali')

the 2067 counterpart of the 2017 grid: six offices, two columns, totals row 'Accumulated scores 236.2'. The offices have moved - Jakarta and Dubai appear, Moscow and Paris survive with different portfolios - so the pair is the paper's only evidence for its own relocation recommendation, and the two grids are otherwise indistinguishable in construction. The measured box again cuts the five-office table below it

the office proposal restated inside the Memo, uncaptioned and introduced only by the sentence 'we hereby propose the optimal location options for new offices'. Six rows, two columns, booktabs, no totals row and no key; its rules run about 80 percent of the text measure, narrower than every other grid in the paper. 'Germany' stands where the language German is meant

the second Memo proposal, and the one measured box in the paper that holds TWO printed tables: both six rows by two columns, booktabs, uncaptioned, separated only by the paragraph 'If your company offers non-necessities'.
